headline: URANIUM TERM PRICE BREAKS 2007 RECORD AT $96.50/LB — US DOMESTIC SUPPLY MEETS JUST 7% OF REACTOR NEEDS
snippet: The uranium long-term contract price reached $96.50 per pound on September 30 — a nominal record surpassing the 2007 peak of $95 — while US reactors sourced only 7% of 2025 domestic deliveries from American mines. A GlobeNewswire release published October 15 argues that proposed US government purchases of domestic uranium could equal the entire current US annual mine output, intensifying competition for limited supply at the exact moment utilities are locking in long-term contracts at record prices. The DOE 'Nuclear Dominance 3 by 33' initiative aims for a fully domestic fuel supply chain by 2033.

headline: RARE DISLOCATION OPENS IN URANIUM — SPOT TRADES 6.7% BELOW TERM PRICE AS URNM FALLS 23% IN 2026
snippet: Uranium spot prices near $89.50/lb now trade at a 6.7% discount to the record $96.50/lb long-term contract price — a configuration ZeroHedge describes on October 16 as a 'rare dislocation' that historically signals a sector re-rating. The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF (URNM) is down more than 23% year to date even as spot uranium held flat for the year and the term price hit all-time highs; the analysis frames Google and Constellation's 20-year nuclear power purchase agreement signed October 6 as a demand signal the equity market has so far failed to price.

headline: ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS CALL STRIKE AT WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE — LAST-MINUTE TALKS UNDERWAY IN CHILE
snippet: About 1,020 supervisors and staff at BHP's Escondida mine — the world's largest copper producer at roughly 1 million tonnes per year — commenced strike action on October 14 after mandatory Chilean mediation failed and the union rejected BHP's offer of a 28 million peso bonus. Last-minute direct talks continued the same day in a bid to reach settlement before the walkout entrenches; a prior supervisors' strike lasted three weeks in 2023. The action is separate from the hunger strike at Antofagasta's Centinela mine already in the news queue, adding a second concurrent Chilean copper supply disruption to the market's risk ledger.

headline: LUCA MINING CLOSES C$211M FINANCING FOR COZAMIN — $290M DEAL TO MORE THAN SEXTUPLE 2027 CASH FLOW
snippet: Luca Mining (TSX: LUCA) completed a C$211 million subscription receipt financing on October 14, clearing the key funding hurdle in its US$290 million purchase of Capstone Copper's Cozamin underground copper-silver mine in Zacatecas, Mexico. The 20-year-producing mine holds proven and probable reserves of 6.7 million tonnes at 1.40% copper and 42.2 g/t silver; once consolidated, management projects 2027 operating cash flow of approximately US$223 million against the company's US$37 million in 2025 — a six-fold improvement driven by Cozamin's low-cost operating profile. The deal is expected to close by year-end 2026 subject to court and regulatory approval.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER HITS RECORD Q3 OF 2.03M AgEq OZ — ZGOUNDER MILL THROUGHPUT REACHES 4,096 TPD
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported record third-quarter 2026 production of 2.03 million silver-equivalent ounces on October 14, up 51% year over year and 21% quarter over quarter. Zgounder in Morocco delivered 1.50 million ounces of silver at 92% recovery — itself a record — while the mill averaged 4,096 tonnes per day, also a record throughput. An additional 0.54 million AgEq ounces came from the Boumadine pyrite reclaim operation; CEO Benoit La Salle confirmed the company remains on track for full-year 2026 production guidance.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS RE-ASSAYS 35M AT 3.26 G/T Au AT MICHELLE ZONE — 15.11 G/T OVER 3M IN HIGH-GRADE CORE
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. (TSX-V: CGM) confirmed a re-assay of historic drill core at the Michelle Zone, Swayze Central, Ontario on October 14, returning 35.00 metres at 3.26 g/t gold including 3.00 metres at 15.11 g/t and 5.00 metres at 6.08 g/t. These results from a 2010-era Red Pine Exploration hole — re-sampled after CGM completed its inaugural six-hole program in September — establish that the system hosts meaningful high-grade gold ahead of targeting the broader Swayze Central hydrothermal corridor.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER DRILLS 31.4M AT 2.11% CuEq IN PIT ZONE — HIGH GRADE FROM 78M DEPTH AT KWANIKA, BC
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSX-V: NWST) reported a 31.4-metre intersection grading 0.92% copper and 1.08 g/t gold (2.11% copper equivalent) starting from just 78 metres depth in the Pit Zone at the Kwanika deposit in north-central British Columbia on October 14. The company plans to tighten drill spacing to 50-metre centres to support resource category upgrades ahead of a preliminary economic assessment; the near-surface location of the high-grade zone strengthens the open-pit case for a deposit still advancing toward its first economic study since its December 2025 drill results.

headline: BRIXTON METALS CUTS BONANZA 195 G/T Au VEIN AT THORN PROJECT, BC — 4.11% COPPER AND 147 G/T SILVER TOO
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) reported a surface sample grading 195 g/t gold, 4.11% copper, and 147 g/t silver from a new vein at its Golden Valley Target within the Thorn Project in British Columbia on October 14. These are grab samples rather than drill intercepts, but the discovery of a new bonanza-grade vein structure at Thorn — a large porphyry-epithermal system already known for high grades — adds a new exploration vector ahead of future drill testing at Golden Valley.

headline: FREEGOLD DRILLS 1.24 G/T Au OVER 213M AT GOLDEN SUMMIT — 5.77 G/T IN 21M CORE AS PFS CAMPAIGN TOPS 58,000M
snippet: Freegold Ventures (TSX: FVL) reported a 213-metre intersection averaging 1.24 g/t gold, including a 21-metre high-grade core at 5.77 g/t, from its Golden Summit project near Fairbanks, Alaska on October 15, as the company's 2026 drilling campaign surpasses 58,000 metres toward a Pre-Feasibility Study. Golden Summit hosts 17.2 million ounces in indicated resources at 1.24 g/t Au, and the Dolphin high-grade corridor driving the infill program has been traced for more than 1.5 kilometres — a scale consistent with PFS-level resource conversion.

headline: LITHIUM AFRICA DRILLS 8.0M AT 1.70% Li2O AT SPRINGBOK, SOUTH AFRICA — DMS PRODUCTION TARGETED FOR H2 2027
snippet: Lithium Africa Corp. (TSX-V: LAF) reported complete assay results from drill hole NB1DD26-004 at its Norrabees I target within the Springbok Project in South Africa's Northern Cape on October 15, returning 8.0 metres at 1.70% Li2O from a spodumene-bearing pegmatite. The result follows the company's September 30 inaugural assay batch (6.0m at 2.27% Li2O) and accompanies a strategic shift toward on-site dense-media separation processing, with first spodumene concentrate production targeted for the second half of 2027 — making Springbok one of the few sub-Saharan African hard-rock lithium projects targeting near-term production.

headline: GOLD MINERS FACE 23% MARGIN SQUEEZE — AISC CLIMBS 16% TO $1,785/OZ AS STOCKS AMPLIFY METAL'S RETREAT 2–5X
snippet: An October 2026 analysis by Discovery Alert argues that gold mining equities face a structural margin compression of up to 23% as all-in sustaining costs rose 16% year over year to an industry average of $1,785 per ounce, while spot gold has retreated approximately $711 from its January 28 record high of $4,873. Mining stocks amplified the metal's losses by a factor of two to five — eroding the leveraged-exposure thesis for investors who expected miners to outperform the metal during this cycle. The October 27–28 FOMC meeting is identified as the next key catalyst that could either confirm or reverse the compression.
